claim: ADA defines hypertension in diabetes as systolic >= 130 mmHg or diastolic >= 80 mmHg, averaged over two or more measurements on two or more occasions.

values.confirmation: average of two or more measurements obtained on two or more occasions

document: 10. Cardiovascular Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
section: Hypertension and Blood Pressure Management — Screening and Diagnosis (body text)
quote: Hypertension is defined as a systolic blood pressure ≥130 mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg based on an average of two or more measurements obtained on two or more occasions.
how_verified: official mirror (PubMed Central full text of the ADA article, PMC12690187; diabetesjournals.org returned 403)
conflicts: WHO (2021 hypertension guideline; WHO hypertension fact sheet) and the Uganda Clinical Guidelines define/treat hypertension at >= 140/90 mmHg; WHO only 'suggests' drug treatment at systolic 130–139 mmHg in people with diabetes (conditional).
